messages.author: cb225dbcfabde750
messages.subject: Support for Non-Mixture Bayesian Nonparametrics
parts:
Hi!,

I use the Indian buffet process (IBP) for my research (https://www.jmlr.org/papers/volume12/griffiths11a/griffiths11a.pdf). As far as I can tell, NIMBLE does not natively support IBP (whereas the Chinese restaurant process, CRP, is natively supported as of version 0.10.0). Are there plans to add IBP functionality in the future?

Relatedly, I also use feature allocation models in which an observation can manifest a varying degrees of a feature (instead of 0/1 as in the IBP, the feature count can be 0, 1, ,2 ...,). These models also have IBP-like representation (e.g. https://papers.nips.cc/paper/2007/hash/6da37dd3139aa4d9aa55b8d237ec5d4a-Abstract.html). Do you recommend any tutorials on how to extend the existing code base to handle these processes, if it's possible?

Best,
Tin

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Support for Non-Mixture Bayesian Nonparametrics
parts:
Hi Tin,

As you've probably gathered from the lack of response, we don't have any active plans in this area. As far as tutorials, the best I can offer is that you can look at the code for our BNP stuff to see if that gives you any ideas of how to implement things. The code we have for defining the CRP distribution (in `BNP_distributions.R`) is straightforward, while the code for MCMC sampling is in the `BNP_samplers.R` file. These are in our GitHub repository (github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/packages/nimble). I will say the sampling code there is fairly complicated because of all the different ways that people could use CRP formulations in a model and wanting to deal with conjugacy. 

Happy to chat further if you decide you want to try to implement something and have questions.

-Chris
